Science 274, published p.1927, Experiment 1 setup: 24 eight-month-old infants; four recurring three-syllable units; 2-minute monotone continuous stream; no pause/stress/prosodic boundaries; within-unit adjacent-pair conditional probability 1.0 versus cross-boundary 0.33
Science 274, published p.1927, Experiment 1 test/results: recurring units versus reordered strings never occurring in that order; longer listening to reordered strings; Table 1
Science 274, published pp.1927-1928, Experiment 2 setup/results: recurring units versus boundary-spanning part-units that had occurred during exposure; longer listening to part-units; Table 1

Science 274, published p.1928, notes 12, 14, 16-21: conditional-probability definition, familiarization-preference procedure, counterbalancing, exact test construction, and no condition-A/B differences
Science 274, published p.1928, Discussion: authors infer rapid acquisition/retention of particular recurring groupings; language-specific versus domain-general mechanism remains unresolved

conditions: continuous synthesized speech containing four recurring three-syllable units concatenated in random order, with no pauses, stress differences, or other acoustic/prosodic boundary markers
within each recurring unit, each adjacent syllable deterministically predicts the next syllable; across unit boundaries, a given following unit occurs with one-third conditional probability
two counterbalanced artificial-stream inventories were used, and the source reports no test difference between those inventories within either experiment
population: 24 eight-month-old infants from an American-English environment in Experiment 1 and a different 24 infants of the same age/environment in Experiment 2
task: listen for two minutes to a continuous artificial speech stream and then complete an immediate familiarization-preference test
Experiment 1 compares recurring three-syllable units with reordered strings whose adjacent order did not occur during exposure
Experiment 2 compares recurring units with boundary-spanning three-syllable strings that did occur during exposure but contained a low-probability boundary transition
temporal_scope: two-minute familiarization followed immediately by 12 self-terminated auditory test trials

nodes.description: two-minute exposure to a monotone continuous stream of four recurring three-syllable units without acoustic boundary cues
adjacent syllable relation inside each recurring three-syllable unit, with conditional probability 1.0 in the exposure corpus
adjacent syllable relation crossing a recurring-unit boundary, with conditional probability 0.33 in the exposure corpus
three-syllable test strings corresponding to recurring units from the exposure stream
Experiment 1 control strings made from familiar syllables but arranged in adjacent orders absent from the exposure corpus

Experiment 2 control strings consisting of the final syllable of one recurring unit followed by the first two syllables of another, so the full string had been heard but crossed a low-probability boundary
immediate auditory preference procedure in which a test string repeats while sustained fixation on a blinking side light controls trial duration
duration of sustained orienting/listening during each test trial
reliable within-infant difference in listening duration between recurring-unit trials and the relevant comparison-string trials
source-inferred post-exposure organization in which recurring three-syllable groupings are represented differently from strings containing absent or boundary-crossing adjacent relations

relations.description: the familiarization stream supplies high within-unit and lower cross-boundary adjacent-pair contingencies while withholding acoustic boundary markers
in Experiment 1 infants listen longer to reordered strings than to recurring units, showing discrimination of familiar versus absent adjacent orderings after the brief exposure
in Experiment 2 infants listen longer to boundary-spanning strings than to recurring units even though the boundary-spanning strings had occurred during familiarization
the Experiment 2 recurring-versus-boundary-spanning contrast differs in whether the first adjacent transition is a high-probability within-unit relation or a lower-probability boundary relation
the familiarization-preference procedure supplies the listening-duration outcome
both experiments meet the source's behavioral discrimination criterion through significant within-infant listening-time differences
the two-minute exposure ends immediately before the test phase

the source interprets the differential listening pattern, especially the recurring-versus-boundary-spanning result, as evidence that infants acquired and retained particular recurring groupings from the exposure structure
